target.title: fix(plugins): recurring plugin-scheduled jobs silently deleted after first post-boot agent turn
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugins that schedule recurring session turns via `api.session.workflow.scheduleSessionTurn` (e.g. a daily sync job) would have their cron job silently deleted shortly after gateway boot — the job never fires again until the next gateway restart re-seeds it, with no visible error (only a low-level `plugins/host-scheduled-turns ... cron service unavailable` WARN).

The trigger: any agent turn, cron isolated-agent run, or the agent-runtime prewarm sidecar calling `ensureRuntimePluginsLoaded` after boot. Each call rebuilt and activated a **replacement** plugin registry without the gateway's `hostServices.cron` wired in. Activating a replacement retires the active registry and runs its plugin host cleanup, which `cron.remove()`s persistent plugin-scheduled jobs before the cron-less replacement's async re-registration catches up — deleting the row with no next occurrence.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Update (2026-07-15, addressing review):** the original version of this PR early-returned whenever *any* registry was active, without checking compatibility with the requested workspace/plugin-scope/config/runtime-mode — correctly flagged in review as unsafe (a later call for a different workspace could keep an unrelated workspace's registry active). Fixed: `ensureRuntimePluginsLoaded` now computes this call's `workspaceDir`/startup-scoped plugin IDs/`loadOptions` first, then calls `getLoadedRuntimePluginRegistry({loadOptions, workspaceDir, requiredPluginIds})` — reusing the existing loader cache-key compatibility rules (workspace, config, runtime subagent mode, required plugin IDs) that already govern normal cache-hit reuse elsewhere — and only skips the reload when the active registry is genuinely compatible with *this* call. Otherwise it still loads a fresh, correctly-scoped registry. No change to the load path when no compatible registry is active.

## User Impact

Plugin-scheduled recurring jobs (daily syncs, reminders, any `scheduleSessionTurn`-based schedule) now survive normal gateway activity instead of silently dying after the first post-boot agent turn. As a side effect, per-turn plugin registry rebuild overhead disappears (we measured the prewarm sidecar dropping from ~150–200ms rebuild to a ~5ms no-op).

## Evidence

**Test (RED→GREEN), original patch:** `skips loading entirely when a runtime plugin registry is already active` in `src/agents/runtime-plugins.test.ts` — fails without the guard, passes with it (original submission).

**Test (RED→GREEN), compatibility-aware revision:** replaced the presence-only regression test with three cases against the updated source: `skips loading when the active registry is already compatible with this call`, `still loads a fresh registry when the active one is not compatible (e.g. different workspace)`, and `passes startup-scoped plugin ids into the compatibility check`. RED confirmed against the pre-revision source (10 failed / 1 passed — mock export mismatch, as expected), GREEN against the revised source (11/11 passed).

**Acceptance criteria from review, all verified locally:**
- `runtime-plugins.test.ts` + `subagent-registry.test.ts` (agents-core): 119 passed
- `active-runtime-registry.test.ts` + `standalone-runtime-registry-loader.test.ts` (plugins): 11 passed
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/` + `trigger-script` (cron lane, includes `run.runtime-plugins.test.ts`): 460 passed / 33 files
- `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts` (gateway): 60 passed
- `pnpm build`: clean, 5m14s, no errors
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`: zero new errors vs unmodified main (one pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts`, confirmed present before this change)
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check`: clean

**Live production observation (long-running deployment of the original patch):** on a gateway running a Google Drive knowledge-sync plugin whose daily `scheduleSessionTurn` job died silently within hours of every boot, the guard produced zero `cron service unavailable` warnings across multiple restarts and days of uptime, and the daily job fired unattended at its next scheduled occurrence, end to end. The cron row survives boot with `next_run_at_ms` correctly set. This deployment is single-workspace, so it did not exercise the multi-workspace compatibility gap the review caught — the revised version above closes that gap while preserving the same observed fix.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted PR** (Claude via OpenCode): root cause diagnosis, fix, and tests were AI-authored under human direction and review; the live-deployment verification above is from a real production gateway. I understand what the code does and am responsible for it. "Allow edits by maintainers" is enabled.
